answer.summary: Parmar recommends a rolling six-month roadmap with clearer near-term commitments and a less-settled second half, shared with enterprise customers in an accessible, approved format. This gives customers visibility while preserving room for teams to respond to new information.

sections.heading: Set different levels of certainty across the roadmap
sections.content: Keep a rolling six-month roadmap and update it every three months. Treat the first three months as an 80% confidence target—about 80% of listed work is expected to get done—and the following three months as a lower-resolution 50% target. The roadmap sits against a published annual strategy. This makes the near term useful for planning without making the full six months a rigid promise.

sections.heading: Make it useful and accessible to enterprise customers
sections.content: Use roadmap reviews with enterprise leaders to walk through the work. Miro also publishes an approved-to-show roadmap as a Miro board for field enablement, with short Talktrack recordings from leaders covering areas such as enterprise, platform, end-user experience, and AI. This gives customer-facing teams a way to share relevant roadmap context.

sections.heading: Protect teams’ ability to adapt
sections.content: The lower certainty in the later part of the roadmap allows teams to pivot based on customer requests, competitive moves, or technology breakthroughs—for example, developments around large language models—without being penalized by customers or internally.
